title: burst synthesis lab journal
content:
Purpose: quick lab notebook for synthesizing arrival bursts that better mimic customer traffic mixes (mix of short chat, long completion, embeddings). Goal: exercise warm-cache + batching interactions, microburst queuing, and fallback routing to smaller quantized variants. This is a personal scratchpad; results rough.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Superimposed bursts (short high-amplitude spikes layered on diurnal baseline) produce much higher p99 penalty than single-distribution bursts because KV cache and batch assembly get out-of-phase.
- H2: A microbatch timeout of 6ms performs well for chat-heavy traffic; for mixed-length (30% long tokens) it increases p95 by ~15% but reduces cost by batching gains.
- H3: Small prefill priming (5-10 warm requests spread over 30s prior to surge) reduces cold-cache tail substantially for 2–10s bursts.

Experiment harness (quick):
- Generator: python-based synthetic driver (local) using two components: base Poisson at lambda=45 qps, and superimposed bursts of Gaussian-shaped arrival envelopes. Additional rare "mega" spikes (0.1% of time) follow a Zipfian magnitude.
- Request mix: 55% chat-short (mean tokens 16), 35% embedding-ish (single vector), 10% long-infer (mean tokens 420, max 1024). Model: rwd-gpt-13b-quant (approx sim) and rwd-gpt-13b-fp16 variant for fallback.
- Cluster: 4 x A100-equivalents, 2 serving processes per GPU, runtime config: batch_max_tokens=4096, max_batch_latency_ms=12, kv_cache_enabled=true, prefill_policy=off unless noted.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency for token-start and token-end (we track start-to-first-byte and end-to-last-token), throughput observed, batch sizes distribution, queue length over time.
- Duration: each run ~15 minutes, we capture 95th percentile metrics across the last 10 minutes to avoid transient ramp.

Run A (baseline): pure Poisson 45 qps, no bursts. Observations:
- p50 token-end: 18 ms (chat-short), p95: 38 ms, p99: 83 ms.
- embedding median: 6 ms, p95 12 ms.
- batch size median: 6 requests, tail 16.
- notes: stable, KV cache hit ~88% for chat-short prefixes.

Run B (single large burst envelope): add Gaussian burst centered at t=300s lasting 20s, peak 2k QPS for 4s, then decay.
- p50 token-end (chat): 22 ms, p95: 210 ms, p99: 1.3 s (severe).
- queue length peaked ~4200, many requests spilled to fallback queue thresholded by dispatcher.
- Batching: median batch size rose to 22 during peak, but batch scheduling delay rose, causing token-latency amplification for short responses.
- Observations: KV cache warmups were ineffective because many requests were from cold users => cache miss spike.

Run C (superimposed microbursts): baseline + frequent microbursts (every 30–90s) of 200–600 qps lasting 2–6s, plus occasional mega spikes.
- p95 steady-state: 42% worse than baseline, p99 dominated by mega spikes: up to 2.1s for chat-short.
- batch size distribution more bimodal: many very small batches (1–2) interleaved with large batches (40+); this bimodality causes scheduler thrash.
- Interesting: throughput across GPUs stayed within capacity, but tail latency increases because of head-of-line blocking in the request queue when a large long-infer starts occupying the runtime (KV cache eviction + long token generation). One long-infer had runtime 13s and blocked a GPU's slice causing downstream queue buildup.

Run D (pre-fill priming): same as C but inject 8 warm prefix requests per expected user cohort over 30s before burst onset.
- p99 improved 20–30% compared to Run C; p95 improved ~12%.
- KV cache hit rose back to ~72% during bursts.
- Tradeoff: small added cost for priming but net tail savings look worthwhile for 2–6s bursts.

Run E (adaptive microbatch timeout = 6ms vs 12ms): toggled max_batch_latency_ms between 6 and 12 under identical microburst pattern.
- 6ms: p95 improved for chat-short by ~10%, p99 slightly worse for long-infer (because fewer long requests were coalesced into large batches -> runtime inefficiency on long-infer paths).
- 12ms: better for long runs but increases short-chat p95.
- Conclusion: adaptive per-route timeout needed; single global setting insufficient for mixed workloads.

Run F (fallback routing to quantized variant on overload): We configured smart routing to shift ~30% of long-infer requests to quantized variant when queue > 1200.
- Result: tail reduced significantly for short-chat because long-infer load on FP16 paths reduced; overall quality for long-infer had minor degradations (not measured here). p99 for chat improved from 1.1s to 0.45s under mega spike.
- Note: this requires careful QoS policy to avoid cascading quality regressions.

Quick charts (ASCII, last 2 minutes of a representative microburst):
- QPS timeline (sample): 45,47,49,60,80,150,320,520,460,300,180,90,60,50,48...
- Batch size histogram (representative): |1: 28%|2-5: 35%|6-15: 22%|16+: 15%|
- Latency spark (p99 in ms over window): 80,82,95,120,310,980,2100,1400,720,260,110,90

Open questions / follow-ups:
- 1) Better synthetic generator? Current method overlays Gaussian envelopes; think about non-symmetric bursts (fast rise, slow decay) and arrival clustering by tenant. Add tenant-correlation to mimic multi-tenant noise.
- 2) Explore per-route adaptive batch timeout tied to observed request-length mix in last N seconds. Can we implement this in the scheduler without oscillation?
- 3) Evaluate cost impact of prefill priming at scale (approx model: priming cost = priming_requests * avg_tokens * price_per_token; need to compare to SLA penalties for tail misses).
- 4) Investigate head-of-line blocking mitigation: explore per-GPU lane isolation for long-infer or early-eject long-running requests to dedicated capacity.
- 5) Measure output quality impact when fallback-routing to quantized variants (automated evals). Link to INF-4187 on JIRA.

Notes to self (short):
- Save the generator script as bench/burst_synth_v3.py (TODO)
- Push small dashboard for batch distribution + queue length + p99 overlay (Grafana panel suggested)
- Sync with Priya on fallback routing policy thresholds and SLO error budgets.

Rough checklist for next runs:
- [ ] implement tenant-correlated generator
- [ ] add non-symmetric burst shapes
- [ ] run cost model for priming at 100k users
- [ ] small A/B to evaluate adaptive batch timeout per route

References & links: see linked_artifacts above. Also refer to notes in /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks/microburst-summaries (draft) and Slack discussion on 2025-01-21.

End of scratchpad. Lots of raw numbers above — re-run with better instrumentation (per-lane queue, scheduler timing trace) before sending to SRE or product.
